meta.scope: Japan batch 3 (deep uniqueness pass) — BOJ Tankan (business sentiment, unique to Japan’s financial monitoring), disaster management White Paper and Reconstruction Agency progress statistics (earthquakes/tsunamis uniqueness), Immigration Services Agency foreign residents and immigration statistics (strict immigration policy uniqueness), plus supporting series. Complements earlier batches for a fuller picture of Japan’s distinctive features. Definition locked; no changes.
meta.strategy_note: User requested depth on Japan’s financial importance, earthquake/tsunami disaster management, and strict immigration. This batch prioritises those unique dimensions while maintaining the rich Report format and ~10–12 size.

candidates.title: Tankan (Short-Term Economic Survey of Enterprises in Japan) / 全国企業短期経済観測調査
candidates.publisher: Bank of Japan (BOJ) — Research and Statistics Department
candidates.description: Quarterly business-sentiment survey of enterprises covering diffusion indices for business conditions, production, employment, prices, and annual projections for sales, profits, fixed investment, and exchange rates. Separate results for large, medium-sized and small enterprises, and for manufacturing vs non-manufacturing. One of the most closely watched indicators in global financial markets for Japanese economic conditions and BOJ policy signals.
candidates.notes: Iconic BOJ survey with global market impact. Large manufacturers’ DI is a headline number for equity, FX and rate markets. Includes inflation outlook of enterprises and (from 2026) planned wage-survey enhancements. June 2026 survey showed large manufacturers’ sentiment at +22. Continuously referenced in BOJ Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices and in international financial commentary. Captures Japan’s unique corporate-sector monitoring tradition.

candidates.title: Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices (展望レポート) — BOJ Policy Board forecasts
candidates.description: Quarterly report containing the Policy Board members’ forecasts for real GDP, CPI (all items less fresh food, and less fresh food and energy), and the assessment of the economic and price outlook that underpins monetary-policy decisions. Includes risk-balance charts and detailed background analysis.
candidates.notes: Central communication vehicle of BOJ monetary policy. Markets parse every nuance of the median forecasts, risk balance and accompanying statement. Draws on Tankan, IIP, CPI, Labour Force Survey, CGPI and many other series. Essential node for understanding Japan’s unique prolonged unconventional-policy era and subsequent normalisation.

candidates.title: White Paper on Disaster Management (防災白書)
candidates.publisher: Cabinet Office — Director General for Disaster Management
candidates.description: Annual White Paper submitted to the Diet under the Basic Act on Disaster Management. Reviews major disasters of the preceding year, progress of disaster-risk-reduction measures, reconstruction status, statistical data on fatalities, damage and preparedness, and forward-looking policy (including Nankai Trough and Tokyo inland earthquake scenarios). 2025 edition featured special focus on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake.
candidates.notes: Unique Japanese institutional product reflecting the country’s high seismic and tsunami risk. Compiles official statistics on deaths, missing persons, housing damage, evacuation, infrastructure recovery and budget execution. Continuously referenced by Reconstruction Agency, local governments, and international DRR partners. Serves as the authoritative annual statistical and policy statement on disaster management.

candidates.title: Reconstruction Agency Progress Reports and Statistics on the Great East Japan Earthquake / 復興の進捗状況
candidates.region: Iwate, Miyagi, Fukushima and affected areas
candidates.description: Ongoing official statistics and progress reports on reconstruction from the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami (and Fukushima nuclear accident). Cover number of evacuees, disaster public housing completion, infrastructure restoration rates, industrial recovery (e.g., manufactured-goods shipments in the three most-affected prefectures), and budget execution. Agency mandate extended to FY2030.
candidates.notes: Japan-specific institutional response to the 2011 triple disaster. Key metrics (evacuees still ~26 000 as of early 2026, 100 % completion of planned disaster public housing and reconstruction roads in non-nuclear zones, slower recovery in certain Fukushima municipalities) are updated regularly and cited in White Papers, Diet reports and international reviews. Captures the long-tail uniqueness of post-disaster management in a high-income, ageing society.

candidates.title: Statistics on Foreign Residents in Japan (在留外国人統計) — formerly Registered Foreign Residents
candidates.publisher: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (Ministry of Justice)
candidates.description: Semi-annual (and previously annual) statistics on the number of foreign residents by nationality/region, residence status, age, gender and prefecture. Tracks medium- to long-term residents and special permanent residents. Record high of 4.125 million at end-2025.
candidates.notes: Primary official source on Japan’s tightly managed foreign-resident population. Top nationalities (China, Vietnam, Korea, etc.), residence-status breakdown (Permanent Resident, Engineer/Specialist, Student, Technical Intern, Specified Skilled Worker) and prefectural concentration (Tokyo ~19 %) are closely watched. Reflects Japan’s unique combination of demographic decline and selective, status-based immigration policy. Continuously cited in policy debates on labour shortages and social cohesion.

candidates.title: Immigration and Residence Management Statistics (出入国管理統計・在留管理)
candidates.publisher: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (Ministry of Justice)
candidates.description: Monthly preliminary and annual statistics on entries/departures, immigration inspections, residence-status examinations, deportation proceedings, and related administrative volumes. Complements the stock statistics on foreign residents.
candidates.notes: Flow counterpart to the foreign-residents stock statistics. Tracks the administrative intensity of Japan’s selective immigration regime (applications, approvals, deportations). Used for policy evaluation of Technical Intern Training, Specified Skilled Worker and other status categories. Reflects the strict, status-based character of Japanese immigration control.

candidates.title: Basic Survey on Foreign Residents (在留外国人に関する基礎調査)
candidates.publisher: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (Ministry of Justice)
candidates.description: Periodic sample survey of foreign residents covering living conditions, employment, language, access to services, and challenges. Conducted to inform ‘coexistence’ policy under the Comprehensive Measures for Accepting and Orderly Coexisting with Foreign Residents.
candidates.notes: Qualitative and quantitative complement to the administrative stock and flow statistics. Results (available in multiple languages) are used to design support measures and to monitor the practical effects of Japan’s selective immigration framework. Reflects the policy emphasis on orderly coexistence rather than large-scale permanent immigration.

candidates.title: Reconstruction Agency — Institutional Framework and Progress Monitoring for Post-2011 Recovery
candidates.description: Temporary government agency (established 2012, mandate extended to FY2030) charged with coordinating reconstruction from the Great East Japan Earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima nuclear accident. Publishes regular progress statistics on housing, infrastructure, industry, evacuation and budget execution.
referenced_by: Diet reports and budget documents on reconstruction special accounts
Prefectural and municipal recovery plans in the three most-affected prefectures
International reviews of Japan’s post-disaster institutional response
candidates.notes: Unique institutional node reflecting Japan’s long-horizon approach to major disaster recovery. Progress metrics (evacuees, public-housing completion rates, industrial shipment recovery in the three prefectures, infrastructure restoration percentages) are updated regularly and form the statistical backbone of official reconstruction narrative. Captures the distinctive combination of high-income capacity, ageing demographics and persistent nuclear-related constraints.

candidates.title: Basic Act on Disaster Management (災害対策基本法) and related institutional framework
candidates.description: Foundational statute that establishes Japan’s disaster-management system, roles of national and local governments, the Disaster Management Council structure, and the requirement for the annual White Paper on Disaster Management. Underpins preparedness for earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions and other hazards.
referenced_by: Annual White Paper on Disaster Management
Reconstruction Agency legal and operational documents
Cabinet Office budget and preparedness measures for Nankai Trough and Tokyo inland earthquake scenarios
candidates.notes: Static legal foundation for Japan’s uniquely intensive disaster-risk-reduction architecture. Continuously cited in White Papers, reconstruction progress reports, and forward-looking scenario planning. Qualifies under the expanded definition via recurring institutional reference; pairs with the White Paper and Reconstruction Agency progress statistics as the disaster-management cluster that distinguishes Japan.
